summary: Clarify routing prioritization when customer requests EU residency and observed cross-region egress latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightHealth Analytics reports intermittent high tail latency (500-900ms extra) on generation requests after enabling EU residency preference. They expected all inference and storage to remain within eu-west, but traces show some requests egressing to us-east for model variant fallbacks and returning with higher round-trip latency.

Impact:
- Increased request P95 from ~220ms to ~1.1s during certain routing decisions.
- Customer worried about data sovereignty guarantees for EU residency setting.

Environment:
- Customer account: enterprise org id: bh-8421
- Production traffic primarily from eu-west region, application pins to model family redwood-rlhf-v1 but uses auto-fallback to smaller quantized variant when capacity constrained.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Set residency preference to "prefer_eu" (not strict) in project routing policy.
2) Send burst of streaming generate requests (~200 rps) with context length ~1024 tokens.
3) Observe request traces in customer app and Redwood request IDs; some traces indicate egress to us-east and increased latency.

Observed behavior:
- ~18% of requests during bursts routed to us-east fallback nodes (compatible model but different region).
- Traces show cross-region TLS handshake + egress adds ~350-650ms.
- Customer worried this violates residency expectation.

Expected behavior:
- With "prefer_eu" customer expected routing to prefer eu-west variants and only failover to other regions in case of hard capacity shortage or outage.

Relevant logs/traces (from customer-provided IDs):
- request_ids: ["req_4f3a9b_eu-20260310-12:22:33", "req_4f3a9b_us-20260310-12:23:01"]
- Example trace link: https://console.redwood.internal/traces/req_4f3a9b_eu-20260310-12:22:33

Notes: Customer included sample HTTP headers showing X-Redwood-Region: eu-west and X-Routing-Decision: fallback_policy=compatible_variant, priority=regional_availability
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage — collected traces and confirmed pattern. Asked SRE for routing policy clarification and whether 'prefer' differs from 'strict'.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Anika Rao): Confirmed smart-routing policy has precedence order: strict_residency -> region_affinity_score -> model_compatibility. 'prefer' sets region_affinity_score but may still choose cross-region if local capacity/burst constraints predict SLA violations. Added timeline and asked for sample scheduler logs.

2026-03-12 - Customer (BrightHealth): Shared request archive and noted that they did not see any explicit capacity errors prior to observed cross-region egress. Asked if TTL for region pinning exists or if ephemeral routing decisions could cause egress for single requests.

2026-03-13 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Investigating: pulled serving-runtime metrics and autoscaler events for customer's dedicated pool. Observed multiple short-lived GPU autoscale cooldowns and model variant promotions triggering fallback to us-east for ~5-20s windows. Pushed for deeper kernel-level logs to confirm eviction vs routing decision.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Region affinity weighting is probabilistic under burst — when local queue depth + estimated tail-latency > policy threshold, smart-router chooses a compatible variant in another region to preserve P95 latency. This matches behavior observed in routing decision header.
Hypothesis B: Short autoscaler cooldowns cause temporary capacity gaps; routing logic may treat that as 'unavailable' and route to fallback region even if overall cluster utilization is moderate.

Evidence: Serving runtime logs (2026-03-10 12:22:30) show model shard allocation delays: 'shard_activate_timeout' entries for node eu-west-03 for model redwood-rlhf-v1. Autoscaler logs show scale-up requested at 12:22:28 and node became healthy at 12:22:49 — ~21s gap.

Tracing: Correlation between shard_activate timeouts and cross-region route increases. Estimated extra egress latency matches observed 350-650ms delta.

Security/residency implications:
- 'prefer_eu' is a soft affinity; it does not guarantee zero-cross-region egress. Only 'strict_residency' setting currently guarantees that routing will avoid cross-region egress unless there is a catastrophic outage. This was not obvious from current docs.
resolution:
2026-03-14 - Support: Provided interim explanation to customer: 'prefer_eu' is a soft preference — during short capacity cold-starts or when predicted tail-latency would breach SLO, the router will choose a compatible node in another region. This is a tradeoff between strict locality and P95 latency.

Workarounds offered:
1) Switch to 'strict_residency' if the customer requires absolute egress locality. Note: strict_residency may result in queueing or 503s instead of routing cross-region in overload scenarios.
2) Reserve Dedicated capacity (predictable pool) in eu-west for mission-critical endpoints to avoid autoscaler-induced gaps.
3) Increase provisioned warm pool or pre-warm the quantized model variants to reduce shard activation delays.

Product follow-ups assigned:
- ENG-ops to add clearer messaging in Console where residency preference is configured (docs ticket CREATED: DOCS-589).
- Infra to investigate autoscaler cooldown heuristic and reduce shard_activate_timeout false positives (ticket: INT-4421).

Customer accepted workaround 1 for now (testing strict_residency on a subset of endpoints) and requested follow-up confirmation post-change.

Post-change verification steps performed: enabled strict_residency on 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC for a canary route (10% traffic). Observed no cross-region egress during subsequent bursts. P95 for canary increased slightly (~+80ms) but satisfied customer's data residency requirement.
